claims.text: Arc melting followed by rapid quenching produces a fully disordered FCC Fe–Mn–Cr–Co–Ni solid solution.
Annealing at 650 °C for 48 h promotes Fe–Cr short-range ordering.
Annealing at 650 °C for 48 h promotes Mn–Ni short-range ordering.
The specified anneal enhances SRO without inducing second-phase precipitation.
Increased chemical SRO homogenizes local magnetic exchange interactions.
Increased chemical SRO enhances magnetoelastic coupling.
Homogenized exchange interactions and enhanced magnetoelastic coupling sharpen the magnetostructural transformation.
A sharper magnetostructural transformation increases the low-field magnetic entropy change.
A sharper magnetostructural transformation narrows thermal hysteresis.
The SRO-enhanced microstructure maintains or improves thermal conductivity.
The SRO-enhanced microstructure maintains mechanical stability.
At 0.5 T, the annealed sample will have at least 20% higher peak isothermal magnetic entropy change than the as-quenched baseline.
The annealed sample will have at least 30% narrower thermal hysteresis than the as-quenched baseline.
The annealed sample will have at least 10% higher thermal conductivity than the as-quenched baseline.
The annealed sample will show no loss in compressive yield strength relative to the as-quenched baseline.
The as-quenched alloy has ΔS_M of approximately 1 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹ at 0.1 T.
The as-quenched alloy has a thermal hysteresis width of approximately 4 K.
The as-quenched alloy has thermal conductivity of approximately 10 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹.
The as-quenched alloy has compressive yield strength of approximately 600 MPa.
The proposed SRO mechanism holds within ±5 at% of equiatomic composition, for anneals at 600–700 °C for 24–72 h, and at applied fields of 0.1–1 T.
